inscriptions on oracle bones are divided into five periods based on time and the lineage of Shang Dynasty kings. The first period was during the reign of King Wu Ding, when the types of sacrificial offerings were numerous and the procedures were complex. However, by the fifth period, as evidenced by the divinatory inscriptions of King Di Yi and King Di Xin, there was a reduction in the number of types of offerings and the procedures were simplified and formulaic. Ancestor worship became the main content of the divination, while there were fewer and fewer divinations to the Sky God and Earth Gods. This paper explores the impact of the development and changes in religious beliefs during the late Shang Dynasty on oracle bone inscriptions and divination practices.
